## Claim — `domain:cli` seat

Session `session_019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`, branch `claude/issue-11301-conversions-only-exit-pin`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` + assignee in one stroke, read back.

**Scope** — triage (`5389800891`): *"Task (S, test-only). Add the fixture that raises a conversion so the documented conversions-only cell (`valid: true, warnings: [], conversions: [...]` ⇒ exit 1 under `--json --strict`) is pinned. The behaviour is deliberate and documented; only the pin is missing."*

⛔ **The behaviour is not on trial.** Every existing fixture raises zero conversions, so that documented cell has never been exercised — the gap is coverage, not correctness. If the pin comes out red against current behaviour, ⛔ do **not** "fix" the code to match the pin: stop and report, because either the doc or the implementation is wrong and deciding which is not this card's.

`Clause-②: no` — test-only.

### ⚠️ A gate landed under you an hour ago

**#11599 (#11341)** just armed: `check:cli-test-child-env` refuses a bulk `process.env` reference in any **spawner** file under `packages/cli/test/**`, over a shrink-only baseline. If your new fixture or its harness spawns a process, use `childEnv()` from `test/helpers/serve-process.ts`. ⛔ Do **not** add a baseline entry for new code — the baseline holds only leaks that predate the gate, and adding to it is the one move that would make the ratchet meaningless on its first day.

⛔ Also do not edit any existing violating file to "help" — those are #11596's, one card per neighbourhood.

### Anti-vacuity for a pin whose whole point is that it was missing

The ablation is not "revert the fix" — there is no fix. Show the pin **discriminates**: with a fixture that raises a conversion, `--json --strict` exits 1; with the conversions removed from that same fixture, it does not. A pin that passes on both sides pins nothing, and that is exactly the shape this card exists to remove.

Prove mutations on disk by grepping both the injected and the removed text (an editor exit code proves nothing; a zero-hit `sed` exits 0), carry `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, predict the split before running, and **report a wrong prediction rather than fitting it**.

### Delivery

Changeset: test-only, likely none — say so and why if you skip it. Push, open a **draft** PR with `Fixes #11301`, run the affected suite plus the repo's fast checks, derive the gate set with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` rather than a hand-built path list, and quote each gate's **own verdict line**. **A gate that refuses is NOT MEASURED.** Keep the report proportionate — this is an S card.

## Review complete on substance — ⛔ arming waits on CI

`domain:cli` seat, session `session_019siH5jDmk5hrayvfyojUqR`. PR **#11609** @ `32ecb986`. At read time `Test Core (1/6)` and `Lint & Repo Gates` were still `in_progress`; everything else green. ⛔ `in_progress` is not `success`.

`Clause-②: no` — test-only, and the file is excluded from published output by `tsconfig.build.json`, which is also why no changeset is correct here.

### ⭐ The card's own suggested fixture was a trap, and it was measured rather than attempted

The issue proposed `object-compactLayout-to-highlightFields`. It is **unusable**: already `retiredFromLoadPath`, so the schema tombstones the key and it raises a validation **ERROR, not a notice** — which would have pinned a completely different cell while looking like the right one.

⭐ That is exactly the trap the issue's own warning flagged, and the dev found it by measuring instead of by trusting the suggestion. Replacement chosen from the 17 registry entries **still live on the load path**, and verified to raise no other advisory (`warnings` length 0) so the pin is not accidentally asserting two things at once. The reasoning is recorded in the test comment, where the next reader will meet it.

### The pin discriminates, which was the whole assignment

Not one fixture but a **pair from one template differing in a single key** on one `page:header` component — `description` (the live subtitle-alias window) versus the canonical `subtitle`:

- first: `valid:true, warnings:[], conversions:[1 notice]` ⇒ exit **1** under `--json --strict`, exit **0** without it, text `--strict` also 1
- second: exits **0** on every face, `conversions: []`

So the pin turns on **the conversion**, not on "a page is present". A single fixture would have left that ambiguity in place, and this card exists precisely because an untested cell reads as covered.

⭐ **And it guards its own future**: `conversions` is asserted **non-empty**, because the chosen entry retires at protocol 18. When that happens the test goes red **with a remedy message** instead of quietly passing on an empty cell — the same "documented but never exercised" shape, pre-empted one turn ahead.

### Anti-vacuity done as discrimination, and predicted down to the assertion

There is no fix to revert, so the ablation made the fixture byte-identical to its canonical twin (`headerPageSource('description')` → `('subtitle')`). On-disk proof both directions plus sha256 (`7cde9871` → `391ebbd5` → `7cde9871`), `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, `git status` clean after.

The prediction was **1 failed / 5 passed, failing on the floor assertion `expect(text.code).not.toBe(0)` rather than the conversions guard, because the floor is asserted first in the body.** Observed: exactly that, `AssertionError: text --strict must fail on the conversions-only config: expected +0 not to be +0`, canonical control green.

Predicting *which assertion* reddens, not just how many, is the version of this discipline that cannot be satisfied by luck.

### Two smaller things done right

**Both refusals reported as refusals.** `check:i18n` and `check:i18n-coverage` first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the workspace CLI is not built` / `Nothing was checked`; measured only after the build, and only the measuring runs are quoted.

**Repo-wide lint was not run, and no narrowed scan is claimed in its place** — *"CI owns it."* ⭐ That is the honest form. A narrowed run presented as a substitute for the farm is the shape that quietly shrinks coverage; declining to claim anything is better than claiming a smaller thing.

**And it checked the gate that landed an hour ago on its own initiative**: `#11599`'s `check:cli-test-child-env` is not in this base and could not reach this diff either way — the file is `packages/cli/src/commands/`, the gate's population is `packages/cli/test/**`. No baseline entry added, no existing violating file touched.
